author: haiku
label: seeded-07r-01
changes: Added a summary that says how the system works today, then how the rollout runs; the first version had no summary and no statement of today's system.

Added a terms list that defines each name a newcomer would not know: old and new engine, usage event log, ledger, payment provider, config service, billing_mode, shadow store, mismatch, nightly comparison job, billing monitor, charge failure rate, rollout tool, rollback record, Finance sign-off.

Diagram: added the gate labels to shadow to both (7 days, 0.1 percent, 5,000 invoices) and both to new_only (14 days, no unresolved mismatches, Finance sign-off). The first version had no gates on its transitions.
Diagram: added the 35-day condition on the path to decommissioned, and the 35-day limit on rollback from new_only. The first version allowed decommissioning with no condition.

Diagram: labelled each rollback entry with who can start it: by hand only in shadow, on-call or monitor in both, and on-call within 35 days or the monitor in new_only. Labelled that the 2 percent rule applies in both and new_only only.

Steps: each mode now says what starts it, what it does, which part holds its data, and what happens when it goes wrong. Failure lines sit inside the steps; the first version had none, so no separate failure table was needed.

Rollback: added the rule that catch_up must happen first when rolling back from new_only, the no-double-charge and no-dropped-charge rule on reconcile, and the rule that steps may be skipped or retried. The first version stated only the step names.
Merged the gate-reset rule into the end of the rollback section and removed the repeated copy of the gates from the notes.
Added a where-state-lives section, since the brief asks for it and the first version only listed pieces.

Kept every stated fact from the brief: the 35-day log retention, the 7-day, 0.1 percent and 5,000 gate, the 14-day and Finance gate, the one-cent mismatch rule, the 2 percent over 10 minutes rule, the 35-day decommission and no-way-back rule, the gate reset, one step at a time with a person making forward moves, and the never-charge-twice and never-drop-a-due-charge rules.

Open questions: added the points the brief leaves unstated (counter storage, scope of the 5,000 minimum, skipped steps per mode, retry exhaustion, whether the two 35-day clocks match, record formats, on-call path, sign-off process). These are not guessed.

Inferred, not stated in the brief: a forward move whose gate is not met does not happen; pause_charging and resume_charging are described from their step names only; the monitor applies only in both and new_only, as the brief states. Only the first two are flagged in the text where relevant.
